Diagnostics and Reporting

Source: vignettes/diagnostics-reporting.Rmd
diagnostics-reporting.Rmd

Overview

diagnostics() gives a compact table for fitted DNN-localized estimators. The method is intentionally fit-object based:

  • it uses retained weights rather than refitting;
  • it uses retained distances only when dx was requested;
  • it uses hidden estimator state for NP, CATE, and PLQR diagnostics;
  • it marks unavailable diagnostics explicitly instead of reconstructing missing inputs from assumptions.

The general fields are available for np_result, cate_result, and plqr_result objects when weights are retained:

  • n_eff, max_weight, and top-weight shares;
  • realized rank radii and weighted distance summaries when dx is retained;
  • tuning metadata when a tuning spec was used.

Estimator-specific fields are added by the corresponding method:

  • NP: weighted outcome mean, standard deviation, and outcome quantiles;
  • CATE: treated/control mass and propensity summaries;
  • PLQR: residual-regressor Gram eigenvalues and condition number.

Diagnostics require W. The default return = "W" keeps it. If a fit was created without weights, refit with return including "W".

Nonparametric Regression 

demo_np <- np_demo_data(n = 120, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)

fit_np <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "ess")
)

d_np <- diagnostics(fit_np)
d_np[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "weighted_mean_y",
  "weighted_sd_y",
  "weighted_y_q50"
)]
#> <dnn_diagnostics>
#>   targets: 1
#>   n_eff  : min=51.8421, median=51.8421, max=51.8421
#>   dist   : available for 0/1 target(s)

For NP fits, weighted_mean_y equals the local mean estimate when the weights are normalized.

CATE Overlap 

demo_cate <- cate_demo_data(n = 150, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 2)

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = demo_cate$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  t_col = "D",
  m_col = "m_oracle",
  e_col = "e_oracle",
  x0 = demo_cate$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "psi", "nuisance")
)

d_cate <- diagnostics(fit_cate)
d_cate[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "treated_mass",
  "control_mass",
  "treated_share",
  "weighted_mean_propensity"
)]
#> <dnn_diagnostics>
#>   targets: 1
#>   n_eff  : min=64.9674, median=64.9674, max=64.9674
#>   dist   : available for 0/1 target(s)

Overlap diagnostics are available when the fit was constructed from treatment and propensity inputs. If cate_dnn() was called with only a direct pseudo_outcome, overlap fields remain present but are marked unavailable.

Experimental PLQR conditioning

All PLQR functionality, including these diagnostics and its specialized plots, is experimental and outside the CATE and regression focus of this release.

demo_plqr <- plqr_demo_data(n = 160, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 3)

fit_plqr <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo_plqr$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo_plqr$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = demo_plqr$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "score", "ess")
)

d_plqr <- diagnostics(fit_plqr)
d_plqr[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "gram_min_eig",
  "gram_condition_number",
  "jacobian_min_singular_value",
  "jacobian_condition_number",
  "theta_vcov_available"
)]

The PLQR Gram diagnostic is based on the localized residual-regressor matrix D - m_D(X). It is an identification and conditioning diagnostic, not a local bread estimate.

Tuning Metadata

When a fit uses tuning = ..., the diagnostics table exposes compact tuning metadata without duplicating the full candidate grid into every row.

fit_tuned <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_dnn_paper(lambda = 1.25),
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "tuning")
)

d_tuned <- diagnostics(fit_tuned)
d_tuned[, c(
  "target_id",
  "tuning_name",
  "tuning_default_s",
  "tuning_grid_n_candidates",
  "tuning_lambda_default"
)]
#> <dnn_diagnostics>
#>   targets: 1
#>   dist   : available for 0/1 target(s)

attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid")
#>   candidate_id computed_key is_default feasible reason status lambda  s
#> 1         s_45         s_45       TRUE     TRUE     ok     ok     NA 45
#> 2   lambda_0p3         s_10      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.30 10
#> 3   lambda_0p4         s_14      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.40 14
#> 4   lambda_0p5         s_18      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.50 18
#> 5  lambda_0p75         s_27      FALSE     TRUE     ok     ok   0.75 27

Use attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid") when you need the full candidate table.

Availability Rules

Diagnostics avoid hidden recomputation.

  • If W is missing, diagnostics() errors and asks for a refit with weights.
  • If dx is missing, distance fields are returned as NA with distance_diagnostics_available = FALSE.
  • If CATE treatment/propensity state is unavailable, overlap fields are present but marked unavailable.
  • If PLQR residual-regressor state is unavailable, Gram fields are present but marked unavailable.

This behavior keeps diagnostics predictable and prevents the diagnostics layer from silently rerunning expensive estimator construction.
